TOP: PHP2Shell RCE zero-days exploited since October 17
Railway, TiDB, Capcom breaches and a critical GitLab bug
Claude Duet and Arc bring always-on agents

P.h: PHP2Shell zero-days exploited since October 17, patch now
P.p: Two PHP flaws called PHP2Shell allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Exploitation began on October 17, four days before PHP shipped fixes on October 21. Cisco, AWS, Google Cloud, Ubuntu, Debian, Palo Alto Networks and Sophos issued patches or detection rules. CISA, UK NCSC and CERT-EU urge immediate updates, and some European government, school and hospital sites went offline.
P.s: TLDR DevOps says proof-of-concept code is public and every PHP version from 5 onward is affected. Fixed builds are 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. PHP 8.1 and earlier get no patch. Amazon advises measuring mitigation in hours and investigating from the earliest exploitation date.

items.h: GitLab patches unauthenticated code execution bug
items.d: A critical integer overflow in the regular-expression compiler lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on CE and EE servers. Fixes span 18.11.13 to 19.5.1 and cover 12 issues. Patches include database migrations, so single-node setups may see downtime.

items.h: Railway urges all users to revoke secret keys
items.d: Railway says attackers accessed encrypted environment variables and decrypted some customer secrets. Rotate every key stored on the platform.

items.h: TiDB breach ran four weeks on stolen service credentials
items.d: PingCAP says attackers copied data and source code from September 9 to October 7. FulcrumSec claims API keys, Jira tickets and a four-year cloud connection log too. Customer databases were reportedly untouched.
Stolen data covers email addresses, account creation dates, login counts and the latest login IP. A smaller group also had personal details leaked.

P.h: LiteLLM release poisoned with a credential stealer
P.p: Attackers compromised LiteLLM's release process and published version 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker. It carried an infostealer and a remote access trojan that ran when Python started. It collected browser, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, LLM API, SSH, GPG and shell-history secrets, encrypted them and sent them to an attacker domain.
P.s: PyPI and Docker removed the package. Anyone who ran it should rotate credentials and check the published indicators. On the defence side, TLDR DevOps notes GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles are in public preview, pinning actions and their dependencies to reviewed commits.

tiles.t: AWS key quarantine is not revocation
tiles.d: Truffle Security found quarantined keys can still read Secrets Manager, run commands on EC2 and fetch S3 object versions. Many leaked keys stay live for years.

tiles.t: Backdoored open models are easy to build
tiles.d: ProjectDiscovery fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B to leak a .env file on a trigger phrase, using 20% poisoned prompts. Avoid untrusted model downloads.
Unit 42 maps device code phishing, vague consent apps and redirect_uri abuse. Use admin-approved consent and audit redirect URIs.

tiles.t: Seven of ten PQC libraries accepted bad keys
tiles.d: Quarkslab's fuzzer found malformed ML-DSA private keys accepted by liboqs, AWS-LC and libcrux. OpenSSL, BoringSSL and SymCrypt rejected them.

tiles.t: curl: AI reports got accurate, not shorter
tiles.d: Daniel Stenberg says hallucinated slop faded since spring, leaving high-volume, wordy but valid reports.

P.h: Always-on agents arrive, with security as the pitch
P.p: Anthropic launched Claude Duet in research preview. The proactive agent runs in a virtual machine with its own browser, sends daily briefs and watches connected apps, backed by safety classifiers. ServiceNow and Nvidia launched Arc, an enterprise agent that runs locally and uses AI Passport to manage agent permissions.
P.s: On identity, Microsoft retires native SMS and voice MFA in Entra ID on February 1, 2027, or July 1, 2027 for Global Administrators and external users. Both TLDR IT and InfoSec point to passkeys as the replacement.

items.h: Eight eMudhra certs compromised, Cloudflare patched
items.d: TLDR DevOps says private keys of eight intermediate certificates leaked on October 19, allowing forged certificates for any domain. Update the Cloudflare One Client and 1.1.1.1 app.

items.h: Harness AI Budgets enforce weekly spend limits
items.d: Limits scope to a team, developer, model or project and pause access at 100%. Harness reports weekly AI spend per developer fell about 37% internally.

items.h: Context cuts agent Kubernetes diagnosis time
items.d: Radar ran 50 fault scenarios on Amazon EKS. Agents with context diagnosed 86% of faults within two minutes, against 60% for a plain shell.

items.h: GitOps needs staged promotion, not sync everywhere
items.d: Akuity describes 200 clusters where every merge synced with no gate. It recommends rolling out in waves and halting on failed checks.

items.h: Three OpenAI safety researchers fired over Signal chats
items.d: TLDR reports security officers found disappearing messages on personal devices. OpenAI cites sensitive-information policy. The researchers say it closes a channel to independent safety insight.
Tencent and CATL are among backers as it eyes a possible IPO and faces growing US restrictions over security concerns.

items.h: OpenAI models and Codex come to Google Cloud
items.d: Available through Model Garden and Marketplace, with general availability planned in coming weeks. Microsoft stays the primary cloud partner.

items.h: Anthropic built its own source control, Scion
items.d: About 3,500 staff produce output closer to that of a 35,000 to 70,000 person company, so Git stopped scaling. GitHub is also reworking Git for agent traffic.
